title: upgrade-attn-flashattnv2-rope-fused-kv-batching-scheduling
author: Ava Martinez
release_notes: Performance: Upgraded attention kernels to FlashAttentionV2 with fused rotary/ROPE ops and KV-cache layout improvements. Expect 15-25% throughput gains on long-context workloads and reduced p95 latency. No API changes.
description:
Motivation: Improve overall inference throughput and tail latency for long-context transformer models by adopting the latest FlashAttentionV2 kernels and fusing rotary/ROPE application into the attention projection. This PR also adjusts the KV-cache memory layout to better support continuous batching and updates the scheduler heuristics to prefer fused kernels and reduce memory copies.

What changed (high level):
- Integrate FlashAttentionV2 kernels with support for batched KV and mixed rotary/ROPE encodings.
- Add fused QKV projection + rotary application kernel to reduce memory traffic and kernel launches.
- Rework KV-cache layout to contiguous blocks for faster GPU memcpy and to enable partial-kv lookups in continuous-batching flows.
- Update scheduler scoring to prefer fused kernels when model config and batch shape match; add adaptive fallback to safe kernels when model length or dtype mismatch is detected.
- Add microbenchmarks and end-to-end perf tests in bench/attn_perf.py and CI perf job.

Compatibility/migration: No public API changes. Runtime will automatically select the new kernels when model metadata indicates compatibility (rotary or rope enabled and supported dtype). Fallbacks preserved for older CUDA/driver stacks.

Checklist: 
- [x] FlashAttentionV2 kernel wrappers implemented and unit-tested
- [x] Fused rotary/ROPE application kernel implemented
- [x] KV-cache layout migration implemented with on-attach conversion for existing caches
- [x] Scheduler heuristic implemented and tested
- [x] Microbenchmarks added and perf CI integrated
- [x] Documentation notes for operators added to runtime docs

Tests and validation:
- Unit tests for kernel dispatch and fallback paths added
- GPU microbenchmarks show consistent throughput improvements (see perf section)
- End-to-end smoke tests on a 30B model with 8k context run in CI perf job

Notes: There was an initial CI failure on pytorch 1.13 image due to an intrinsic name collision in the custom kernel build; fixed by renaming the symbol and adding a guarded define. The perf job was rerun and passed.

Related: ENG-2024 contains the roadmap and perf targets for long-context attention work.

review_comments: Liam Chen: Left high-level comments on scheduler heuristics. Please add a microbenchmark comparing fused vs unfused for short vs long context (addressed).
Priya Nair: Verified KV layout change with local reproducer; asked for an on-attach conversion path to avoid invalidating existing worker caches (added).
Diego Alvarez: Noted potential memory fragmentation in corner cases; suggested an extra alignment pass (implemented).
Ava Martinez: Reply: addressed review comments, added additional unit tests for fallback kernels and updated perf numbers in PR description.
perf_summary: Microbenchmarks: long-context (8k) throughput +22% (1.22x) end-to-end; p95 latency reduced by 18-25% depending on batch size. Short-context (<=128) sees minor regression in single-stream latency (~3%) due to slightly larger kernel setup; scheduler falls back to non-fused kernel in those shapes.
notes: Follow-up: schedule rollout as canary on dedicated clusters for one week and monitor token-level latency and error rates. Add a telemetry flag to opt-out if needed. Also plan to upstream small kernel fixes to the FlashAttention repo for maintainability.
changelog_entry: Upgraded attention kernels to FlashAttentionV2 with fused rotary/ROPE ops and KV-cache layout improvements. Improves throughput for long-context workloads and reduces p95 latency. (PR #812345)
